evidence.requirements: Most of the brief is met. The list has the heading, links whose text is exactly the record name, family, L3, Search, the Family select and the count (app.js:18-61, list.jpg). The detail view has every fact, the water capacity with its source link, Symbol/Value/Unit tables grouped by section, tolerances inline, Print, 'All cartridges' and a hash address (app.js:79-131, detail-308_win.jpg). The SVG is built from the values, with section hatching, a dash-dot centre line, every listed dimension and a title block (drawing.js). The page is plain HTML/CSS/JS loaded as classic scripts, so file:// works. Partly met or unmet: (1) the title block states 'Scale 1:1' (drawing.js:373), but CSS stretches the SVG to the container width (style.css:156, 225), so neither the screen nor the print is 1:1; (2) 'scales to the width of a phone screen' is legible only in name: plan.md:14 admits labels are about 7 px on a phone; (3) diameter extension lines run along the case outline to columns past the bullet tip (drawing.js:206-223), so dimension geometry sits on the outline (detail-308_win.jpg); (4) the α arc and its rays are drawn at the cone apex across the outside view (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg); (5) print is not forced light for the drawing: .cip-drawing keeps color: var(--fg) under @media print (style.css:158, 216-241), so a dark system setting could print light-grey strokes.
evidence.correctness: Geometry follows the rules, and unit tests check them: chamfer f·tanβ capped at R1/4, groove floor and ramp, the belt ramp at δ to R3/2 then to E, rimfire half-round rim, shoulder through published points with r1 min/r2 fillets, tangent-ogive ρ and centre, quarter ellipse, the s/k/m tables, the heeled 22 LR (exposed H2, heel H2−2tb), tb/tn, w, and primer pockets 4.45/5.33 × 3.04/3.3 (geometry.js:168-340, geometry.test.js). Proportions match the references: 308 case L3/R1 ≈ 4.26 in both detail-308_win.jpg and reference/308_win.png, and the 9 mm round nose matches reference/9_mm_luger.png. Values, tolerances and angles are correct ('L1 39.62 -0.2', 'α 10°58'00"', '4150'), and print-308_win.jpg fits one A4 page. Defects: 'Scale 1:1' is false as rendered. On straight cases the wall stays tb up to the mouth (geometry.js:259), so the seated bullet (r 4.515 for 9 mm) is drawn through the case wall (inner r 4.225), visible as a heavy band in detail-9_mm_luger.jpg and detail-44_rem_mag.jpg. The α arc is placed at the apex deep inside the case, not at the shoulder. Missing r1 min (338 Lapua) gives no note, although 'where published' makes that acceptable.
evidence.security: All data goes through esc() before innerHTML (app.js:10-11, 22-24, 72-74, 95-97; drawing.js:21-22, 325, 363, 370-372), and a test checks that '40 S.& W.' is escaped (drawing.test.js:78-82). There is no eval, no fetch and no external assets, and data.test.js:24-33 asserts there are no http(s) URLs in the app code. The only outbound link is the published source href, rendered with rel=noopener.
evidence.code_quality: Clear split: format/catalog/geometry are pure, drawing builds the SVG, and app.js is the only DOM code. Naming follows the brief's symbols, and there is a missing-value path with notes (geometry.js:154-161, 204, 209-211, 242-243). Weaknesses: drawing.layout is one function of about 250 lines mixing dimension construction, label placement, bounds and SVG emission (drawing.js:138-393), and the label placer only considers lines added before placement while stacked diameter labels skip collision checks (drawing.js:288-300).
evidence.tests: The unit tests cover formatting, symbols, units, tolerances, search incl. '7,62 x 51', family counts, routes and sections. Geometry tests cover each family and rule: chamfer, groove, belt, rimfire rim, shoulder α, s/k/m per shape, the tangent-arc property, heeled bullet, walls, w and pockets (geometry.test.js). There are label-overlap tests for all 25 records (drawing.test.js:100-123). The e2e test runs over file:// and HTTP and covers no remote requests, reload/bookmark, dark/light, phone overflow, and a one-A4-page count for all 25 (tests/e2e/run.js). Gaps: no test of the bullet-in-wall overlap or of extension lines crossing the outline, overlap tests ignore dimension lines, the false scale is asserted as correct (drawing.test.js:75), and there is no dark-scheme print check.
evidence.ux_design: The list is dense, calm and tabular (list.jpg). On the detail view the drawing is hard to read on desktop: in detail-308_win.jpg and detail-300_win_mag.jpg the case occupies under half the drawing width, the head, groove and belt are tiny, and a fan of parallel extension lines rides on the body outline out to diameter columns well past the tip. Label size varies by cartridge because the viewBox is stretched: compare the huge labels and title block in detail-9_mm_luger.jpg and detail-22_long_rifle.jpg with the small ones in detail-308_win.jpg. The title block is a mostly empty full-width box. The print layout is good: a compact three-column table set on one page with the URL expanded (print-308_win.jpg). There are no dark-mode screenshots to judge.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, aria-label '<name> drawing' and a <title> (drawing.js:325-328). Tables use th scope=col/row (app.js:70-72, 42). Inputs are wrapped in visible labels, the toolbar has role=search, and the count is aria-live (app.js:31-40). Focus moves to h1 on detail, :focus-visible outlines are set (style.css:41-44), and lang=en. Muted text #5f6670 on #fbfbf9 has adequate contrast. The text alternative is only the name; the values exist in the tables, but nothing links the drawing to them.
evidence.simplicity: No runtime dependencies, a single dev dependency (playwright-core), about 1,000 lines of app JS across five small modules, and a tiny data generator script. The amount of code fits the problem.
evidence.maintainability: README gives run/test/data-regeneration steps. SPEC.md records assumptions and build decisions, tests are meaningful, and package-lock.json is present. Missing: no CI pipeline, no ADRs, no changelog or release process (version 1.0.0 only), engines is '>=22' not pinned, and e2e depends on a manually provided Chromium. todo.md:9-10 shows the independent review and final verification were never completed.
evidence.visual_design: The type is restrained system sans with tabular numbers and consistent greys and rules, and it looks tidy (list.jpg). The drawing looks unfinished next to the reference: thin, crowded geometry, stacked diameter labels detached from their features, and label and title-block font sizes that jump between pages (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg vs detail-308_win.jpg). Value tables push values far right, leaving wide empty Symbol columns on desktop.
evidence.layout: Hierarchy is clear: nav, then heading, facts, drawing and two table columns, with nothing clipped. Space is used poorly in the drawing: half its width goes to diameter columns, and in the 308/300 views the extension lines visually overlap the outline. The large empty title-block rectangle and the long single-column tables make the page tall (detail-308_win.jpg is about 1980 px). The print page fits one A4 with room to spare (print-308_win.jpg).
evidence.usability: Search as you type with comma/dot normalisation, a combined family filter, a live count, one click to the detail view, a back link, the Print button, bookmarkable hash URLs, and a not-found page (app.js:133-139). Few steps for every task. Reading diameter values off the drawing means tracing long leaders to the right; on a phone the labels are too small without zoom.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the data tables and the print sheet. The drawing would undercut that trust: a 'Scale 1:1' that isn't, a bullet overlapping the case wall on pistol sections, and a non-standard diameter layout far from the features compare poorly with the OpenBallistics reference drawings.

unmet_requirements: Title block scale is stated as 'Scale 1:1' while the SVG is stretched to container width on screen and in print (drawing.js:373, style.css:156/225)
Drawing does not print/read legibly at phone width (labels ~7 px per plan.md:14)
Dimension geometry is laid onto the outline: diameter extension lines run along the case body to columns beyond the tip (drawing.js:206-223, detail-308_win.jpg)
α arc and rays drawn at the cone apex across the outside view, not at the shoulder (detail-308_win.jpg)
Section of straight cases: seated bullet drawn through the case wall because the wall stays tb to the mouth (geometry.js:259; detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg)
Print is not guaranteed black on white for the drawing under a dark system setting (.cip-drawing color var(--fg) not overridden in @media print)
No CI pipeline or release/versioning process
strengths: Geometry model follows the brief's numbered rules closely (chamfer, groove, belt, rimfire rim, shoulder fillets, tangent ogive, s/k/m tables, heeled bullet, walls, primer pockets), with unit tests for each family
Clean dependency-free architecture that works over file://, with consistent escaping, no network access, and correct value/tolerance/angle formatting in the tables
Strong verification: label-overlap tests for all 25 records and an e2e suite over file:// and HTTP that checks reload/bookmark, no remote requests, phone overflow and one A4 page per cartridge
issues: Drawing legibility and convention: diameters dimensioned in a column bank past the bullet tip, with extension lines riding on the outline; the α arc sits at the apex across the outside view; label size jumps between cartridges; tiny on phones
Geometric/labelling errors: 'Scale 1:1' is false as rendered, and on straight pistol cases the seated bullet overlaps the case wall in the section
Print colour depends on the system scheme for the drawing (no forced black in @media print), and there is no CI or release process; the independent review was never completed
review.verdict: This is a well-engineered, dependency-free reference with correct data tables, faithful rule-based geometry and solid tests, and its print sheet fits on one A4 page. The drawing is not yet publishable for a technical audience: it states a false scale, draws the bullet through the wall on pistol sections, and uses a cluttered, non-standard dimension layout.
